body:
You are currently in charge of a large multinational company. You have many projects in hand. There are N employees currently in your company, all of whom have an unique ID, numbered from 1 to N. You want to form a non-empty set of teams of equal sizes from these employees such that each employee works in exactly one team. Your task is to find the number of ways to form such sets of teams.

Two ways are different if there exists at least one pair of employees who are in same team in one way but belong to different teams in the other way.

There is an interesting property of N: it can be expressed as p1*p2, where both p1 and p2 are prime numbers (p1 may be equal to p2) and Max(p1, p2) < 10*Min(p1, p2). You need to output the number of ways modulo q, where q will always be a prime number.

Input

The first line of each input contains a single integer T, which denotes the number of test cases. Each case starts with a line containing two integers, L and q, where L is the number of lines to follow and q is a prime number.

Each of the next L lines contains a single integer N.

Output

For each test case, output “Case <x>:” in a separate line, where x denotes the test case number. Then for each line containing N, print the number of ways modulo q. Follow Sample Input and Output for details.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ T ≤ 5
  • 1 ≤ L ≤ 20
  • 1 < q < 5000
  • 1 < N < 1012

Example

Input:
2
3 1013
4
6
10
2 11
6
9

Output:
Case 1:
5
27
60
Case 2:
5
7

Explanation

For the first case, first line, we have N = 4. The different ways in which the employees {1, 2, 3, 4} can be divided into equal-sized teams are:

  • { {1} , {2} , {3} , {4} }
  • { {1, 2} , {3, 4} }
  • { {2, 3} , {1, 4} }
  • { {2, 4} , {1, 3} }
  • { {1, 2, 3, 4} }

    • You can verify that these are the only 5 possible ways. And since 5%1013 = 5, the answer is 5.

    All submissions for this problem are available.
